Hillary Supporter Lady Gaga Paid $21,000 By Clinton Campaign

I just want to help put this in perspective.

Campaign finance laws exist. If you were a cook, and you decided to host a fundraiser for your candidate, your time counts as a campaign contribution. Campaigns are only allowed to accept so much money from an individual by law. The amount that you would typically charge, multiplied the amount of time you spent, still counts as a contribution.

Performers, on the other hand, are in a land of limbo regarding the law. If your notoriety is as a performer, your main source of income is talking/singing. So if you show up to events and talk on behalf of your candidate, does that count as a campaign contribution? After all, you typically charge $20,000 dollars for a public event.

There have currently not been any legal challenges for celebrities showing up at these events, but with the world looking at Hillary's potential legal issues, it seems it is wiser to "hire" the celebrity, pay what their fees would normally be, and not test the waters of a law that is murky at best.

Remember, Lady Gaga gets a fee for just showing up at places, so her appearance counts as a campaign donation. Her time needs to be reimbursed in order to stay safely on the right side of the law.
